Subject: MAP kickoff: Acme Health — perf benchmarking scope and ask

Sara —

Thanks again for the sync today. As discussed, attached is a compact MAP-focused benchmarking plan so we can align on acceptance criteria and timelines before the procurement queue. High-level goal: validate that Redwood can meet Acme's latency and concurrency targets for long-context workflows (8k–32k tokens), and show TTFT and tail-latency behavior with KV cache enabled.

Key asks from Acme we want to capture into the MAP (please confirm):
- Target TTFT: <= 250ms for first token on median prompt (8k context)
- 99th percentile token latency target: <= 300ms under normal load
- Concurrency target: sustained 80 simultaneous sessions during peak hour
- Representative prompt set: 250 sample prompts across 8k / 16k / 32k context splits (you mentioned the docs team will provide these)

Planned Redwood deliverables in the MAP:
1) Evaluation plan & test harness (we will provide a reproducible script and instructions)
2) Bench results CSV (P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, TTFT)
3) KV cache hit analysis and recommendations (config knobs: prefix caching, shard size)
4) Close timeline and go/no-go decision points (we propose a 3-week cadence)

Deliverable timeline proposal:
- Wed (May 13): Redwood reproduces a dry-run on sample prompts and posts baseline numbers.
- Fri (May 15): Full benchmark run with target concurrency and KV configs; share CSV + heatmaps.
- Tue (May 19): Review call, action items, and final MAP sign-off for pilot.

Attachment: MAP_action_items_v3.xlsx (outline + responsibilities).

If any of the Acme targets above need adjustment, flag them here and we will update the MAP doc.

—Jonas

On Thu, May 13, 2026 at 08:24:00 -0700 Jonas Weber wrote:
> Team —
>
> Forwarding Acme's clarifications (see Sara's reply). Action items for Redwood engineering so we hit the Fri run:
> - Aditya: please run dry-run on the 30-sample prompts (attached) and post baseline P50/P95/P99, TTFT, and tokens/sec. Include KV cache on/off. Estimate: 4 GPU-hours.

Quick summary of the Friday benchmark (dry-run -> scaled run):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated test cluster (A100x2), model: rwd-open-13b-v2 (float16), sequence lengths tested: 8k / 16k / 32k (prompt+gen), KV cache: on / off, concurrency: single-session dry-run, then scaled to 80 sustained and 150 burst for 5 minutes.
- Artifacts attached: latency-results.csv (detailed per-request rows), brief notes PDF (embedded in MAP_action_items_v3.xlsx).

Key numbers (median of N=1,200 requests per bucket unless noted):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): 8k: P50=185ms, P95=240ms, P99=320ms
- Token generation latency (per-token) @ steady-state (8k prompts): P50=18ms, P95=38ms, P99=82ms
- Tail latency under burst (150 concurrent for 5m): P95(TTFT)=410ms, P99(TTFT)=720ms; observed CPU saturation on host during bursts.
- Throughput: tokens/sec (aggregate per GPU): 8k prompts: 1,100 tok/s; 16k: 850 tok/s; 32k: 430 tok/s.
- Concurrency behavior: sustained 80 sessions — system maintained P95(TTFT) ~ 280ms; bursts to 150 caused P99 spikes as above and ~12% request retries in the driver at peak (retries due to transient timeouts).
- KV cache impact: enabling KV cache reduced average token-latency by 22% for prompts with repeated context (measured on 30-sample set). Cache population time for a 16k prefix averaged 75ms; hit rate stabilized ~62% after first pass on the corpus.
- Resource notes: 32k runs reached 86% GPU memory and increased host RSS; recommend configured spill-to-disk threshold or model sharding for sustained 32k loads.

Recommendations for MAP:
1) For pilot, accept TTFT P50<=200ms (we hit 185ms) and contractual P95 <=300ms (we are ~240ms baseline but 280ms under sustained concurrency). For procurement, call out burst P99 behavior and proposed mitigations.
2) Enable KV cache with prefix caching enabled; this yields ~20–25% latency reduction on repeated-context workloads.
3) For 32k target SLAs, propose dedicated larger GPU profiles (or model quantization to int8) and set a soft-limit on sustained 32k concurrency.
4) Add automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model variant during sustained bursts to protect P99s — include in MAP as a mitigation action.

Next steps:
- Grace to produce the full harness and replay logs by Mon (May 17).
- Jonas to share the short procurement summary to Acme and schedule the Tue review call (May 19).

Attachments referenced: latency-results.csv, MAP_action_items_v3.xlsx, acme_prompt_samples.jsonl
